ARCHITECTURE: this city has TWO independent networks under one city id. Edinburgh Trams T50 is a genuine hub-lock at Edinburgh Waverley (Waverley area stop, separate from the National Rail station) with confirmed termini Newhaven and Edinburgh Airport. National Rail is ALSO hub-locked to Edinburgh Waverley (EDB CRS, main station, 20 platforms) with Haymarket and Slateford as through-running satellite stations on the same hub, not separate hubs (unlike Glasgow's two independent NR termini). doNotGroup applies at Waverley specifically: the Trams stop and the National Rail station are physically near each other but are separate platforms/infrastructure with no automatic interchange described in the report.

doNotGroup is required: Edinburgh Waverley — Trams (Waverley area stop) vs Edinburgh Waverley — National Rail (EDB CRS, main station). Separate platforms, separate infrastructure, different operator, no automatic interchange per the report (line 3, 17, 41, 73).

Neither the Trams line nor the National Rail hub needs INTERNAL doNotGroup the way London Bridge/Liverpool Street did in london-se-national-rail: the report gives no evidence of separate platform/boarding-section logic per operator at Waverley (ScotRail/LNER/Avanti/CrossCountry/TransPennine share one flat departure board, distinguished by destination + operator), same posture as Glasgow Central and Glasgow Queen Street.

Edinburgh Trams T50 is a POINT-TO-POINT LINE WITH CONFIRMED TERMINI (Newhaven, Edinburgh Airport) and a stated 7-10 minute headway (report line 38, 49) — unlike Glasgow Subway (closed loop, no termini). Standard line+terminus direction label applies; see direction-model-memo.md Part 1.

Trams real-time status: UNKNOWN. TFE Open Data API is closed/inactive; no successor confirmed (report line 61, 79-81, 103-109). Schedule-only v1, skip risk flagged by Nico and carried forward here unresolved. Do not assume real-time is available.

Trams stop ORDER is NOT independently verified by this pack. The oracle report's line 21 list gives 23 named stops in a plausible end-to-end reading, but the report never states this list represents an ordered stop sequence, and no official Edinburgh Trams map or GTFS stop_times dump was consulted by Nico or by this pack. Per this lane's guardrail against guessing at a station graph, the 'stations' array below is carried in the report's list order AS A CANDIDATE ONLY, explicitly flagged unverified — see hazard-pack.md and direction-model-memo.md.
Timezone Europe/London HAS DST (BST/GMT). Not a separate Scotland timezone.

City lands as 'Coming Soon' (status stays planned; no separate coming-soon enum in registry.js) until (a) National Rail is unblocked (DARWIN_LDB_TOKEN) and (b) the Trams real-time question is resolved with Transport for Edinburgh — whichever finishes wiring first still leaves the other mode schedule-only or absent; Jim's call at D2.

License: Trams (DFT BODS) confidence 'clear' for static GTFS (OGL 3.0), 'not found' for real-time (no feed confirmed). National Rail (Darwin/OGL 2.0 + NRE amendments) confidence 'unclear' on third-party rider redistribution, same open item as every other UK NR region. National Rail static GTFS (Transitland, CC-BY-2.0 UK) is reference-only, confidence 'clear', not used to derive this catalog.

Falkirk High boundary: recorded in hazard-pack.md's dedicated consistency-check section. This pack does not add Falkirk High to Edinburgh's catalog — Edinburgh's own oracle report never lists it as an Edinburgh station, and Glasgow's merged pack independently excludes it too. The two reports' phrasing of *which region owns it* differs (Glasgow's report says 'owned by Edinburgh region'; Edinburgh's report says it is 'Glasgow's boundary station') — flagged back to Nico/Tim rather than resolved here, since neither pack actually claims the station either way.
